confusable_with.discriminator: Completeness is not the goal at this phase. The operator needs to know they are at risk; nobody needs their state published while an engagement is still being aimed.
The object is named. It is only the state that is held back.

cues.name: Verbal notification carrying a longitude window
cues.presentation: A verbal notification to operations centres on a developing direct ascent event.
cues.means: The verbal call carries the affected longitude window, not the individual target names. The written report carries the names.
cues.first_action: Give the longitude range. Names go in the written product.

confusable_with.cue_id_or_name: Giving the same content on both channels
confusable_with.discriminator: A deliberate asymmetry. The verbal notification travels faster and less controllably, so it carries the window rather than the names.

cues.name: Apogee marginally above the belt
cues.presentation: An ascending object whose maximum altitude sits a little above geosynchronous altitude.
cues.means: There is a tolerance band. Within about fifty kilometres above the belt the apogee point is still the centre longitude; beyond it the ascending penetration point is.
cues.first_action: Compare the maximum altitude against the belt plus the tolerance before choosing the assessment longitude.

confusable_with.cue_id_or_name: Treating belt altitude as a hard line
confusable_with.discriminator: An apogee a few tens of kilometres above the belt still uses the apogee longitude. Only a materially higher apogee switches to the penetration point.

cues.name: No object tracked on the expected trajectory
cues.presentation: Sensors search the posted trajectory and find nothing.
cues.means: The trajectory is an estimate. Search around it before concluding there is nothing there.
cues.first_action: Extend the search along track by several minutes either side and across track by a few degrees, rather than reporting no detection.

confusable_with.discriminator: A state vector converted to a trajectory carries error in both time and geometry. Absence on the exact line is expected, not informative.

cues.name: Handover brief missing next step or checklist position
cues.presentation: An event briefed at changeover with its history and reporting covered, and no statement of what happens next or where in the procedure it currently sits.
cues.means: The incoming operator must re-derive both from a thread they have not read, under time pressure. Two of the six briefing points are missing and they are the two that carry forward.
cues.first_action: Ask for the next step and the current checklist step before accepting responsibility.

confusable_with.discriminator: Thoroughness about the past is not the same as clarity about the next action. Check the six points, not the length.

cues.name: Tasking elevation with no expiry recorded
cues.presentation: A rank change entered in the running record without an expiry date against it.
cues.means: The elevation will become permanent by omission, because nothing will prompt the step-down.
cues.first_action: Add the expiry when the elevation is made, not later. The reason and the expiry travel with the object.

confusable_with.discriminator: There is no indefinite elevation. The top ranks are temporary tasking, so if the need is ongoing, that is a standing rank change rather than an elevation.

cues.name: Record updated only at changeover
cues.presentation: A shift approaching handover with the running record largely untouched since it began.
cues.means: The handover is already compromised. What gets briefed will be what is remembered rather than what happened.
cues.first_action: Update through the shift. Handover quality is decided hours before handover.

confusable_with.cue_id_or_name: A quiet shift with little to record
confusable_with.discriminator: A shift briefed as quiet has been recorded as untrue more than once. Absence of entries and absence of activity are different things.

cues.name: Daily task allocated to another cell
cues.presentation: A routine daily task that this cell has not performed today.
cues.means: Either it belongs to another cell on this day, or it has been missed. Those look identical from inside one cell.
cues.first_action: Check the allocation before assuming coverage. A task assumed covered by someone else is the commonest way a routine check quietly lapses.

confusable_with.discriminator: Allocation varies by cell and by weekday. Read it rather than recall it.

cues.name: Delta column carrying natural drift
cues.presentation: A verified manoeuvre determination shows a large right ascension change and a moving argument of perigee alongside very small changes in period and semi-major axis.
cues.means: Almost nothing. The delta column reports change across the fit interval, and over a fit spanning a day or more the node regresses and the perigee rotates on their own. The large numbers are natural drift and the small ones are the manoeuvre.
cues.first_action: Read the fit interval from the time row, then ask which of these elements would have moved anyway over that span before attributing any of them to a burn.

confusable_with.discriminator: A plane change puts the energy into inclination and shows a right ascension change out of proportion to the natural rate for that orbit. Natural regression matches the rate you would compute for the orbit and the interval.

confusable_with.cue_id_or_name: CUE-001 residual departure from the zero line
confusable_with.discriminator: The residual says the object left its state. The determination table says what the new state is. Neither on its own tells you which element the burn touched.

cues.name: Elevation with no spare collection capacity
cues.presentation: An object has just been raised into the ranks that attract dedicated collection, and the schedule shows no rows for it from the constrained sensor type while every existing tasked object still has its own.
cues.means: The elevation has been recorded but not resourced. Dedicated capacity is fixed by contract, so an addition requires a removal, and until someone decides which object loses custody the new tasking exists only on paper.
cues.first_action: Name the object to be de-tasked, and take the decision to the mission area lead rather than leaving the request open.

confusable_with.discriminator: A geometric gap closes on its own as the pass geometry comes round. A capacity gap never closes, because nothing was taken away to make room.
An outage removes rows for every object on that provider. A capacity shortfall removes them for the newest object only.

cues.name: Target element set in a proximity report
cues.presentation: A draft proximity report carries appended element sets for the actor and for the object being acted against.
cues.means: Possibly a disclosure error. Whether the target's element set may be appended depends on what the target is, not on whether the data is held. Against a friendly target it is withheld; for a protected object or a well-tracked uncorrelated track nothing positional is published at all.
cues.first_action: Establish what the target is before the report is published, and strike the appended set where the rule says it does not go.

confusable_with.cue_id_or_name: Withholding a state early in a direct ascent event
confusable_with.discriminator: That withholding is by phase and is released once the engagement is committed. This one is by the nature of the target and does not relax.

confusable_with.cue_id_or_name: An element set omitted for staleness
confusable_with.discriminator: A stale set is a quality problem and is fixed by getting a fresher one. A disclosure withholding is not fixed by better data.
